related_issues.reason: Closed as completed: 'Sign published executables for Windows' (antivirus-driven signing request). Same signing theme, but this issue adds version-resource metadata (Product Name, Company Name) and targets the pip-installed uv.exe, so it is not the same request as far as the search excerpts show.
Closed as completed: macOS code signing request for uv/uvx. Same class of distribution-trust request on a different platform.
Open: Windows AV scanning delays for unsigned uv binaries. Shares the unsigned-binary trust theme, but the symptom is startup latency, not publisher metadata.
Closed as duplicate, labelled external: Windows Defender false positive on uvw.exe. Related trust/SmartScreen-adjacent symptom, different request.

rationale: The reporter asks for uv.exe to carry Windows version-resource metadata (Product Name, Company Name) and a signed publisher certificate. That is a request for new behaviour, so enhancement, which matches the template label. Nothing in the report is a defect in uv or another tool. Searches for Windows metadata, code signing, SmartScreen and version resources found no open issue asking for exactly this. Closed #10336 (Windows signing) is the nearest match, but I could not confirm from the excerpts whether it covered pip-installed binaries or metadata, so I list it as related, not duplicate, and confidence is medium. Earlier signing work (#10336, #14870) suggests the maintainers already consider signing in scope, so a maintainer should check whether the pip wheel path is covered.
